mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 0.3% in the same month signals a dual labor market deterioration, which amplifies recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential demand, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of HOUST below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling Real Final Sales (RSAFS) and a rising Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% in the same month signals stagflation, which erodes real purchasing power and corporate pricing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during months with both RSAFS falling and CPIAUCSL > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 3% during a recessionary regime (UNRATE > 6%) signals a monetary policy easing intended to stimulate growth, which historically has been associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes where FEDFUNDS falls below 3% and UNRATE > 6%.
